title: Confidence gain versus error reduction for budgeted dementia assessment
status: Locally frozen analysis plan before new model evaluation; not a public preregistration
primary_endpoint: Concurrent CDR greater than zero at first observed visit; not biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer disease or future progression
csf_endpoint: Recorded Alzheimer diagnosis versus mild cognitive impairment among symptomatic participants; supplementary task
primary_comparison: Brier-gain gate minus continuous certainty-gain gate in Brier score at 30% capacity; negative favors Brier gain
certainty_gate_target: Indicator abs(p_full-0.5)-abs(p_basic-0.5)>0.2, learned from cross-fitted training predictions
gate_models: Regularized logistic regression for certainty gain; ridge regression alpha=10 for Brier gain; basic features only
reporting: AUROC, average precision, Brier, log loss, balanced accuracy, macro F1, sensitivity, specificity, missed positives, referrals, calibration bins, subgroup counts and errors
data_rules: Never pool OASIS releases or call them independent external validation
Fit imputation and scaling inside every training fold
No CDR or Group as OASIS predictor
No outcome/progression fields as CSF predictor
No synthetic PET or cross-person joins
Capacity ranking uses pretest features only
Test set never used for tuning
limitations: Diagnosis may incorporate cognitive and CSF measures
MRI features are volumetric summaries rather than image encoders
Retrospective feature acquisition simulation, not actual clinical utility
No clinical deployment or first-ever novelty claim
protocol_amendment: After development-only evaluation: add continuous certainty gain with the same ridge learner as Brier gain, to isolate the surrogate target and avoid a sparse fixed-threshold comparator. Preserve original binary certainty gate as secondary. No final-test metrics were accessed.
continuous_certainty_target: abs(p_full-0.5)-abs(p_basic-0.5), fit by ridge alpha=10 on training cross-fitted predictions
